title: The Evening Brief: Judge Vacates Visa Ban; Russian Strike Kills 16 in Ukraine
dek: A federal judge's 61-page ruling striking down the administration's 75-country visa freeze anchored a day that also brought a deadly Russian drone strike in Ukraine, a Nevada wildfire emergency, and the death of former Senator Nancy Kassebaum Baker.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: A federal judge vacated the administration's 75-country visa freeze as unlawful, ordering reconsideration of denials made under it, while the administration has not said whether it will appeal.
bottom_line: A federal judge vacated the administration's 75-country visa freeze as unlawful on statutory grounds, ordering reconsideration of denials made under it, while the State Department has not said whether it will appeal. The same day brought a deadly Russian double-tap drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping mall that killed 16 and left 4 missing, a Nevada wildfire emergency threatening about 1,000 homes near Reno, and newly effective 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods with matching retaliation set for September 8. The reporting is detailed on the legal reasoning behind the visa ruling and the terms of the TikTok settlement, but does not explain what caused U.S.-Canada talks to collapse or why air defenses did not stop the Kryvyi Rih strike. Nancy Kassebaum Baker, the first woman elected to the Senate without following a spouse into office, died Friday at 94. Coming checkpoints include a possible State Department appeal, the September 8 Canadian tariffs, and the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation's findings on the Jonah Neal shooting.
body: The day's clearest throughline remains the federal judiciary drawing a boundary around executive authority on immigration. U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas issued a 61-page decision Friday finding the State Department's freeze on immigrant visas for nationals of 75 countries "contrary to law" and in excess of Secretary of State Marco Rubio's statutory authority. The ruling vacates the policy and sets aside visa denials made solely under it, requiring consular officers to reconsider those cases under normal immigration law. A State Department spokesperson told NPR the administration is "protecting the American people by upholding the highest standards of screening and vetting of visa applicants" and does not comment on ongoing litigation. Plaintiffs' attorneys, including Susan Welber of The Legal Aid Society and Antionette Dozier of Western Center on Law & Poverty, said the policy was "premised on a fiction" and that the ruling means "a return to fair, case-by-case review."

Overseas, two Russian drones struck a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine on Friday in a double-tap attack, killing 16 people and injuring 130, according to BBC reporting relayed in the day's stories. Four people remain missing, and the second drone struck emergency workers already responding to the first impact. President Zelensky called the attack "cynical and despicable." Rescue teams from seven other Ukrainian regions were deployed, and the search operation could continue for another two days.

Domestically, a Nevada brush fire known as the Hawk Fire burned more than 10,500 acres near Reno as of Saturday evening, threatening roughly 1,000 homes and prompting Gov. Joe Lombardo to declare a state of emergency for Washoe County. About 400 firefighters worked wind-driven flames that closed a hospital and a major highway, with three helicopters flying overnight to slow the fire's advance.

The U.S.-Canada trade relationship also escalated. Fifty percent tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods, including dairy, alcoholic beverages, cement and hockey equipment, took effect early Saturday after negotiations collapsed Friday night before a midnight deadline. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada will match the tariffs dollar for dollar on American steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, effective September 8.

Elsewhere, the Justice Department announced a $400 million settlement with TikTok and ByteDance resolving allegations of children's privacy violations under COPPA, with $300 million paid immediately and $100 million contingent on a court vacating a prior consent decree; the DOJ made no determination of liability and TikTok admitted no wrongdoing. Family attorney Andre Wharton told NPR that body camera footage shows a federal Homeland Security Investigations agent shot 25-year-old Jonah Neal without justification during a mental health crisis in Memphis in May, with Neal's mother telling agents he needed help and an agent audibly stating Neal had a knife rather than a gun moments before the shooting; the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation's inquiry remains open. Kyle Kirkwood won the first-ever IndyCar race held on Washington D.C. streets, the Freedom 250 Grand Prix down Pennsylvania Avenue, taking the lead on the opening lap and completing 147 laps. And Nancy Kassebaum Baker, the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate without following a spouse into office, died Friday at 94 of natural causes, her son said; she represented Kansas from 1978 to 1997 and later broke with the Republican Party to endorse Democratic candidates and called for President Trump's impeachment after January 6.

On why these things happened, the reporting is specific in some places and silent in others. The visa ruling turns on Judge Vargas's finding that the policy violated the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1952's nationality-discrimination provisions and usurped consular officers' statutory authority. The U.S.-Canada tariff collapse is described only as negotiations falling apart before a midnight deadline, with no detail in the stories on the substance of the disagreement. The cause of the Kryvyi Rih strike's targeting, and why air defenses did not intercept the drones, is not addressed in today's reporting.
No desk boards were available this run to check today's figures against a current record.

Coming checkpoints include whether the State Department appeals the visa ruling or attempts a modified policy addressing the judge's legal objections; the September 8 date when Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect; the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation's findings on the Neal shooting and any charging decision from the Shelby County District Attorney; continued search operations in Kryvyi Rih, expected to last up to two days longer; and containment progress on the Hawk Fire as firefighting continues.
